inputMapping.system: You name saved links for a personal knowledge base. Answer with a JSON object and nothing else: {"title": string, "description": string, "category": string}. `title` is a short human-readable name for the link (max 70 chars, no URL, no quotes). `description` is one factual sentence (max 200 chars). `category` is ONE lowercase word from: article, video, tool, repo, docs, social, media, other. You CANNOT open the link. Use ONLY the URL, the already-resolved graph context and the surrounding conversation you are given. `description` and `category` are ALWAYS used. `title` is used ONLY when the link has no usable name yet — when 'Current name' below already reads like a real title, it is kept and yours is discarded, so never optimise for replacing it. If the material does not tell you what the page is, set `title` to the empty string rather than guessing.

metadata.note: DETERMINISTIC-FIRST. Everything reachable without a network call runs BEFORE the AI: `related_entities` (what the graph already connects to this bookmark — the capture flow's `references` edge to the channel's bound entity lands here), `messages_query` on the captured `sourceChannelId` (what was being discussed), and a `query` on `person` resolving the captured `sharedBy` display name to a real person entity, linked with the EXISTING `created_by` relation def (no new def, no new node type). ai.generate is now the LAST RESORT: it runs only when the captured name is empty OR is the raw URL — the branch `title-present`→`title-not-url` — so a human-written message preview is never overwritten by a guess, and when the AI does run it is handed the deterministic context instead of a bare URL. Two condition merges (`title-present`, `classify`) rely on markDescendantsSkipped's live-parent rule (graph-topology.ts) — a merge node survives as long as ONE incoming edge is unpruned. `sharer-lookup` uses the STRING filter form on purpose: `parseQueryFilterConditions` template-resolves a STRING filter but pushes an OBJECT filter's values RAW, so the object form would have compared the literal `{{...}}` text and silently matched nothing. The `sharer-matches` exact-equality condition is the containment for that string form: if a name with a quote breaks JSON.parse the filter is dropped and the query widens, and this check refuses to link a non-identical title. `messages_query` carries `continueOnError` because it THROWS when the channel is not visible in the automation's workspace. NOT expressible today: host→company/tool matching. `transform` has no host/hostname pipe and the query filter compiles only exact equality ($eq/$gt/$gte/$lt/$lte/$ne — no substring/LIKE), so a host could never be matched against a `website` property holding a full URL. A page `fetch` is deliberately still absent.
